question_text: Which of the following unit fractions is the smallest in value?
step_by_step_solution: For unit fractions (numerator 1), as denominator n increases, the value 1/n decreases. Since 8 > 5 > 3 > 2, 1/8 is the smallest.

question_text: In Brahmagupta's addition formula a/b + c/d = ____ / (b.d).
step_by_step_solution: Brahmagupta (628 CE) converted fractions to a common fractional unit: a/b + c/d = (a.d + b.c)/(b.d).

question_text: Jaya's school is 7/10 km from home. She travels 1/2 km by bus and walks the rest. How far does she walk?
Jeevika takes 10/3 minutes to run a lap; Namit takes 13/4 minutes. (a) Who is faster? (b) By how many seconds?
step_by_step_solution: (a) Convert to common denominator 12: Jeevika = 10/3 = 40/12 min; Namit = 13/4 = 39/12 min. Namit takes less time (39/12 < 40/12), so Namit is faster. (b) Difference = 40/12 - 39/12 = 1/12 minute = (1/12) x 60 seconds = 5 seconds.
